beats: A strip of plastic bottle and two cable ties. This leak fix shouldn't hold.
The secret: those ties squeeze the pipe harder than the water pushes out.
Inside, tap water pushes outward at about three bar, forty-three psi.
First, the bottle strip wraps the pipe and covers the hole like a soft gasket.
Then each tie is pulled tight, about ten kilograms of pull, twenty-two pounds.
Wrapped around a curve, that pull turns into a squeeze pointing inward, all the way round.
The tighter the curve, the harder the same pull presses in.
And a thin tie puts all that force on a narrow strip.
On a twenty-two millimetre pipe, that's about nineteen bar, two hundred seventy-five psi.
Six times harder than the water pushing out.
So the plastic stays pinned shut, and the water never lifts it.
Leak fix: the squeeze beats the push, six to one.
Cogwise: how things work. Follow for the next one!
